text:
alex: Heads-up — I ran a quick smoke on the new Karpenter provisioner config for GPUs in us-west-2. Observed two issues: 1) cold-start latency on p4d is spiking, 2) fallback to p3 is not triggering when p4 spot pools are exhausted.

marta: Hmm. Did you set the preferential ordering in the provisioner constraints?

alex: Yes, provisioner has providerPreferences: [p4d, p4, p3]. The logs show attempts for p4d, then timeouts, but Karpenter doesn't try p3 until the timeout window passes (2m). That kills request latency.

li: That's expected — Karpenter waits for node readiness before trying the next provider. We should shorten the acquisition timeout for GPUs or add a fallback policy.

devon: What about adding a conservative quick-fail path for interactive workloads? i.e., if pod has annotation karpenter.cloud/fallback=immediate, try next provider after 15s.

marta: I like that. Could be opt-in so batch jobs still prefer waiting for ideal hardware.

alex: Agreed. Also saw network attach delays when instances come up with ENI provisioning in the subnet. That adds ~30s before kubelet registers. Could be why we miss the latency SLO.

ops-bot: alert: GPUProvisionerENIFailures increased by 3 in us-west-2 in the last 15m.

li: For ENI delay we can try enabling secondary IP preassignment and increase CNI warm pool size. In AWS, attaching ENIs and IPs is a big contributor.

sierra: Also worth evaluating the use of GKE autopilot-like VPC native config? But changing networking across clusters is a big migration. Might be out of scope for this sprint.

alex: Can we at least do two things short-term: 1) reduce provider acquisition timeout to 30s for annotated pods, 2) add a fallbackPolicy that triggers p3 immediately when p4 spot capacity is not reported?

marta: Yes. I'll prototype a patch to the provisioner controller. Need to be careful about thrash — frequent rollovers could cause consolidation churn.

devon: Add a rate limiter on fallback actions: max 1 fallback per node-group per minute. Also ensure we annotate fallback reason for observability.

li: For consolidation — we should run a simulation with our workload trace. Last time consolidation windows of <10m caused pods to bounce. Let's keep window at 20m for now.

alex: Also cost check: p4d on spot is ~3x p3 spot. Fallback to p3 reduces cost but may affect model perf (batch size restrictions). Need per-model SLO flags.

marta: Good point. We'll respect pod annotation karpenter.cloud/gpu-family-preference and karpenter.cloud/quality-tier (best-effort | guaranteed). That way models that need p4d can block fallback.

osm-team: quick question — how will this interact with Dedicated mode? We don't want Karpenter to provision into Dedicated pools accidentally.

li: We can constrain provisioner to specific node labels and taints. Dedicated pools will have taintdedicated=true:NoSchedule. Karpenter provisioner won't touch those unless pod tolerates.

sierra: Test plan: 1) unit tests for timeout/fallback logic, 2) canary deploy provisioner to staging, 3) run synthetic cold-start load (100 short-lived pods) and measure 95th latency before/after, 4) run consolidation sim.

alex: I'll prepare the kustomize overlay. For quick testing, here's a snippet: 
```yaml
provisioner: 
  ttlSecondsUntilExpired: 60
  providerPreferences: [p4d, p4, p3]
  acquisitionTimeoutSeconds: 30 # for annotated pods
  fallbackPolicy: 
    enabled: true
    immediateFallbackIfSpotExhausted: true
    rateLimitPerGroupPerMin: 1
```

marta: Nice. Add a feature flag (alpha) behind karpenter.experimental.gpuFallback so we can toggle without rollout.

devon: I'll own the rollout and monitoring. We'll add these metrics: fallback_attempts_total, fallback_success_total, fallback_rate_limited_total, enic_prepare_time_seconds histogram.

alex: For alerting thresholds: if fallback_rate_limited_total > 5 in 5m or enic_prepare_time_seconds p95 > 45s, page eng-infra.

ops-bot: incident runbook: GPU provisioner fallback — /runbooks/gpu-provisioner-fallback.md (created draft).

marta: I'll open a PR with the patch + tests + runbook link. Tagging @devon for rollout and @li for networking changes.

sierra: Thanks all. If staging looks good, let's schedule a short maintenance window for prod canary next Tue. :calendar: 

alex: Sounds good. I'll post the kustomize overlay and load script in this thread when ready.

marta: marking follow-ups: - PR, - staging canary, - consolidation sim, - cost regression check.

osm-team: thanks — will coordinate with Dedicated ownership to ensure taints are respected.

devon: Adding task to runbook: how to manually force fallback for a pod: `kubectl annotate pod <pod> karpenter.cloud/fallback=immediate`

alex: closing the loop — moving to a ticket in JIRA: INFRA-8421. I'll attach logs and the ENI snapshot.
